chunks.title: JavaScript Fetch API
chunks.text: The Fetch API makes it easy to retrieve data from an external source.

chunks.title: JavaScript Fetch API
chunks.text: Here's the basic syntax.

chunks.title: JavaScript Fetch API
chunks.text: The first parameter is the URL that will provide the data.

chunks.title: JavaScript Fetch API
chunks.text: The second parameter is optional and is an object containing options.

chunks.title: JavaScript Fetch API
chunks.text: In this example, we are retrieving a list of to-do tasks.

chunks.title: JavaScript Fetch API
chunks.text: Fetch is promise-based, so we will use .then to get our response.

chunks.title: JavaScript Fetch API
chunks.text: The response contains our headers and data.

chunks.title: JavaScript Fetch API
chunks.text: In order to consume the data, we will need to convert it into JSON.

chunks.title: JavaScript Fetch API
chunks.text: So we return response.json.

chunks.title: JavaScript Fetch API
chunks.text: Once that is returned, it will move into the next .then and now we can do something with

chunks.title: JavaScript Fetch API
chunks.text: the JSON data.

chunks.title: JavaScript Fetch API
chunks.text: This example will return 200 to-do tasks.

chunks.title: JavaScript Fetch API
chunks.text: In this next example, we are only asking for the to-do task with the ID of 1.

chunks.title: JavaScript Fetch API
chunks.text: In our console, we will see the ID, title, completion status, and user ID.

chunks.title: JavaScript Fetch API
chunks.text: By default, without any options, Fetch uses the get method.

chunks.title: JavaScript Fetch API
chunks.text: We can also use other methods with Fetch.

chunks.title: JavaScript Fetch API
chunks.text: That's where the options come in.

chunks.title: JavaScript Fetch API
chunks.text: In this example, we are going to create a new to-do task.

chunks.title: JavaScript Fetch API
chunks.text: After our URL, we will include our options object.

chunks.title: JavaScript Fetch API
chunks.text: The first option will be the method, and we will use post.

chunks.title: JavaScript Fetch API
chunks.text: Next we'll include the data that we want to send in the body.

chunks.title: JavaScript Fetch API
chunks.text: In order to send it properly, we have to wrap it in JSON.stringify.

chunks.title: JavaScript Fetch API
chunks.text: And lastly, we include our headers option with our content type set to application.json.

chunks.title: JavaScript Fetch API
chunks.text: After that, we have our first .then that receives the response and processes the JSON.

chunks.title: JavaScript Fetch API
chunks.text: Then our second .then can do something with the response data.

chunks.title: JavaScript Fetch API
chunks.text: In this instance, we receive the data that we sent along with an ID that the server added.

chunks.title: JavaScript Fetch API
chunks.text: Initially there were 200 entries, and now there are 201.

chunks.title: JavaScript Fetch API
chunks.text: There are other factors to consider when using Fetch, such as error handling.

chunks.title: JavaScript Fetch API
chunks.text: Note that if you receive an error status such as a 404 error, Fetch will still resolve successfully.

chunks.title: JavaScript Fetch API
chunks.text: So you will need to do some extra error handling.

chunks.title: JavaScript Fetch API
chunks.text: This has been a 90-second JavaScript January.

The second parameter is optional and is an object containing options. In this example, we are retrieving a list of to-do tasks. Fetch is promise-based, so we will use .then to get our response. The response contains our headers and data. In order to consume the data, we will need to convert it into JSON. So we return response.json. Once that is returned, it will move into the next .then and now we can do something with the JSON data. This example will return 200 to-do tasks. In this next example, we are only asking for the to-do task with the ID of 1. In our console, we will see the ID, title, completion status, and user ID. By default, without any options, Fetch uses the get method. We can also use other methods with Fetch. That's where the options come in. In this example, we are going to create a new to-do task. After our URL, we will include our options object. The first option will be the method, and we will use post. Next we'll include the data that we want to send in the body. In order to send it properly, we have to wrap it in JSON.stringify. And lastly, we include our headers option with our content type set to application.json.
